The Medium click is his.** The operator's bar for publishing is a cold read of 9 of 10 or better. Six reads on 16 Nov, one per version, graded 5, 6, 6, 5, 6 and 6; the sixth is the first that answers "publish as it stands" with yes. What still separates the reads from 9 is evidence and not prose (the table below), and neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1821 owns it.

**Direction taken under Nightshift (22:30Z):** the post goes to its stranger read and its one fact check now, aiming at Wed Nov 18, and the missing evidence becomes a follow-up post. Three gates of the operator see that decision before anything is public: the merge of neomjs/pages#94, the merge of this pull request, and the Medium click. An objection at any of them holds it.

Part 3 of *How an AI team remembers*, re-planned on 16 Nov around the measurement of neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1800, its repair (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1820) and a BM25 check (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1821): the post `learn/blog/codebase-knowledge-base-for-ai-coding-agents.md`, its `blog.json` entry and the series lines in parts 1 and 2. The first screen says who writes and who merges, and gives the balanced-40 numbers for one search: vector search 15; the same grep hits ranked by match count 10, by distinct words 30, by BM25 34; the RAG index 26 in the afternoon and 33 after the fix that evening, a tie with BM25 that the first screen calls. Then: what was tested; the three rankings with an eight-line shell function and a short BM25 script; the three flaws the test found and their fix the same evening; where the index wins and where it is stale (between them the two find all 40), split by freshness and by question style; limits; and a scorer for the reader's own questions. Title: *Codebase RAG vs grep for AI coding agents: the same grep hits scored 10, 30 or 34 of 40.*

Reader: an engineer who uses coding agents every day on a large codebase and has never heard of Neo. Should want: to know whether their agent's first search finds the right file, and a cheap way to check. Action: run `bm25rank.py` and `rgscore` on ten of their own questions.

Evidence: L1 (docs; rendered on the portal dev server; the three scripts run as printed) → L1 required. Residual: none. Merge order: neomjs/pages#94 (the two images) first. agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline jobs run in CI.

| 6 | `7b81f04553` | 6 | Yes: "honest, short, runnable"; no fix blocks | `bm25rank.py` on five questions, 20 minutes | a title scoped to the measured claim; the owed questions on a re-ingested index; a hybrid row and plain unranked `rg` |

- **The scripts as printed**, in one directory that holds worktrees of neo `459371e353` and neo-agent-brain `a2a621cb78`, with a tab-separated export of the 40 questions (answer files joined by `|`): `rgscore` prints 30 of 40 for `rgrank`, and the same loop with `python3 bm25rank.py` prints 34 of 40. The same holds for `bm25rank.py`'s row format, for a named root with and without a trailing slash, for a path with a space, under bash 3.2 and zsh 5.9. On the 40 questions the totals are unchanged: 30 for `rgrank` and 34 for `bm25rank.py`, with the runner's ripgrep exclusions and with none.
